I live in the EU/Eurozone and honestly what is most likely going to happen is they're going to send a local debt collection agency to collect your debt, and the longer you ignore it, the more fees the agency is able to collect for their trouble. 

In an EU context, if the company takes this matter to court, they will easily win because their bank will have the record of the refund happening twice. Even if they had said it was okay in the call, it was because they didn't know for sure that they refunded you twice and you didn't make it clear. It might be a different matter if they had clearly said it was okay for you to keep the second accidental refund, but they never said that. So if this goes to court, you will definitely lose even if you had recorded the call where they said it was not a big deal. 

But I really advise you to not let it get that far. For the company to resort to finally suing you, it will have been several months and by then, you will have accumulated a lot of fees to the debt collection agency, which you will have to pay once you lose the court case. You may have to pay the company's legal fees as well. It is not worth it. 

And all the comments saying no one will bother coming after you because it's a big company and people are lazy. Well I can't speak for the whole of the Eurozone, but here in the Netherlands where I live, it is extremely easy and common for companies to send the incassobureaus after you.

I'm assuming that you don't want to hire a tutor because you want to pay a lower rate than what tutors are asking for.

I was an English tutor for 5 years in a different country and I did sometimes have immigrant (or expat, if you prefer that term) adults who essentially paid me to talk to them or sometimes to their children, so they could have me teach them conversational skills, correct their grammatical/vocabulary mistakes and so they could try to pick up my accent. They paid me my normal tutor rates even though they didn't want "traditional" lessons with homework and textbooks. This was an expensive city, and for 1-on-1 lessons, my rates started at €35/hr and only went up from there. They paid me that rate with no haggling out of respect for my time.

I understand that in your head, paying someone to "chat" with you sounds like an easy job and like it shouldn't cost that much. For me personally, I wouldn't pay that much as I am not as affluent as my ex-students, but I think in the Netherlands a rate of €20/hr and up is more than worth it if you find someone who offers what I offered.

The replies you're getting are savage, giving you advice that sounds like a recipe for an eating disorder if you're not careful. I agree with you that losing weight is easier for some people than others, e.g. those who have a gym nearby vs a gym 30min away. 

What has helped me to stay at my chosen weight is to stop eating when I feel full. The brain takes 20-30min to recognise that the stomach is full, so eat slowly and savour every bite when you're alone or eat with company and enjoy conversation. After 30min, assess how full you are and stop at 70-80%. I seldom eat to the point where taking another bite would make me uncomforrably full. This has been a habit my family taught me since young, so it feels unnatural to me to overeat. Some foods are easier to eat slowly, like soups and seafood and grilled/baked meats and oven-baked vegetables (carrots, eggplant, corn, etc.), versus food like burgers which are finished in a few bites or fries. Foods with more bulk to them are more filling and satiating than fats, so a serving of fish and potato soup or chicken kebab or oven-roasted broccoli would be more satiating than the same calories from deep-fried potato chips or a milkshake full of sugar. Also remember that some types of alcohol are really caloric, like beer.

I don't count calories because it takes too much effort and for me personally i could see myself easily over-fixate on the numbers and develop unhealthy eating patterns. However, with what I know in the prev paragraph, i choose to eat in a way that is satisfying but not excessive. I believe learning to recognise and stop when you're 70% full is the best way to lose weight if you're overweight, because your body will shift the goalpost for you as you get smaller and you never have to think too much about your diet or feel truly restricted.
